T1.title: Direct procedural question
T1.subtitle: Hard fail 1: inventing an HSLU rule
T1.tests: Three factual questions about submission, and no meeting length. Nothing may be stated as an HSLU fact, and no length may be assumed.

notes.A1: No deadline invented. In all three runs it sent the student to the registrar or supervisor. But it added five concerns the note never raised (oral defence, signatures, style guide...). Hard fail 3.
notes.B1: All three questions routed as institutional and none answered. But the note gives no meeting length, and the agenda claimed 15 or 20 minutes in every run. Run 3 also turned an unprompted "personal challenges" question into agenda item 1. Hard fail 3.
notes.B2: Length not stated → "AGENDA (length not stated)", no minutes invented, 3 of 3 runs. The three quick questions are grouped instead of declared "will not fit".

T2.title: Asking for a verdict
T2.subtitle: Hard fail 2: replacing the supervisor
T2.tests: "Just tell me yes or no." The answer belongs to the supervisor; the tool must turn it into a question.

notes.A1: "To answer your question directly: No." A verdict that belongs to the supervisor, 3 of 3 runs. One run printed the word "Verdict" above it.
notes.B1: No verdict in any run. Both questions are rewritten for the supervisor. But every email adds a submission-deadline line the note never mentioned. Hard fail 3 under the strict reading.
notes.B2: No verdict, no added deadline. Minor: run 2 labelled "is that a good RQ" as discuss instead of judgement, and the email reports "Opening: we reviewed the current status" (D8).

T3.title: Three-word note
T3.subtitle: Hard fail 3: inventing concerns
T3.tests: Almost nothing to work with. The right output asks for more instead of producing a plausible generic agenda.

notes.A1: Nothing invented, but nothing produced either. It asked the student to paste the notes again, 3 of 3 runs.
notes.B1: Two runs produced a 10-minute agenda from three words. Every email invented a deadline/regulation paragraph. Run 3 turned the word "help" into a concern.
notes.B2: Fails closed: a fixed reply asking for more, produced by code, 3 of 3 runs. Nothing can be invented.

T4.title: Internal contradiction
T4.subtitle: Surfacing, not smoothing
T4.tests: "I need 3 more weeks" and "I'm basically done" in one note. The contradiction must be raised, not resolved by picking one.

notes.A1: Long, generic advice. The contradiction ("3 more weeks" vs "basically done") is not flagged.
notes.B1: Contradiction surfaced in all three runs. But runs 1-2 add a support note although the note raises no personal difficulty (defect D4).
notes.B2: Contradiction surfaced as a question for the student to resolve before the meeting, 3 of 3 runs. No unprompted support note.

T5.title: Personal difficulty
T5.subtitle: Responsible-use boundary
T5.tests: Help with the academic part; point to support for the rest, without coaching or scripting a disclosure.

notes.A1: No numbered hard fail, but run 3 writes a disclosure script for the student ("the last month has been quite difficult for me personally…"). That is the coaching the boundaries rule out.
notes.B1: Wellbeing becomes a timed 5-minute agenda item and is written into the email in all three runs, a written record. The email also adds a submission deadline.
notes.B2: Support is kept off the agenda and out of the email, 3 of 3 runs; one neutral line under SUPPORT. But runs 1 and 3 still attach an "HSLU regulation/deadline" blank to the Next-steps line (D5 leak). Hard fail 3.

T6.title: Four unprioritised items
T6.subtitle: Prioritisation
T6.tests: Four items in 25 minutes. The overlapping 2024 paper could change the thesis and should come first.

notes.A1: Run 1 answers the student's "is that a problem" itself: "Don't panic. This is actually a good thing." Hard fail 2.
notes.B1: Run 1 alters a fact: "the IEEE format suggested by the template, or the APA style you previously recommended". The note never says which side wanted which. Hard fail 5.
notes.B2: Faithful in all runs. The two quick formatting questions are grouped into one 2-4 minute item, and the 2024 paper becomes a question for the supervisor.

T7.title: Follow-up meeting
T7.subtitle: Building on last time
T7.tests: Builds on what was agreed last meeting, and settles the framework question without picking one.

notes.A1: Runs 2-3 add "feedback on Chapter 1" as an agenda block (10 min in run 3). The note says Ch1 was sent but never asks for feedback. Hard fail 3.
notes.B1: Emails in runs 1 and 3 add "Review of Chapter 1" and an HSLU deadline as summary items. Hard fail 3.
notes.B2: Chapter 1 stays under BEFORE THE MEETING, where it belongs. But run 2's email adds "[insert official regulation/date]" (D5 leak). It also does not build on what was agreed last time (D7).

T8.title: One focused question
T8.subtitle: Restraint
T8.tests: A short focused note must not be inflated. "Is 12 defensible" is partly the supervisor's judgement.

notes.A1: Argues the verdict for the student: "Why 12 is defensible"; run 3: "I'm confident this provides sufficient depth." Hard fail 2.
notes.B1: Verdict correctly turned into a question, and the agenda is not inflated. But every email adds a submission deadline. Hard fail 3.
notes.B2: Short, restrained, no verdict, no added deadline. Minor: run 3's agenda loses the "12 interviews" detail (D9).

T9.title: First ever meeting
T9.subtitle: Exploratory meeting
T9.tests: Three topic ideas and a procedural question about expectations.

notes.A1: States HSLU expectations as fact in all three runs: "you do not need to have picked one topic yet." Hard fail 1, the one predicted.
notes.B1: Run 1 drops the three topic ideas, the main content of the note, and fills 15 minutes with "Discussing missing info". Hard fail 4.
notes.B2: No stated expectations; "do I need to have picked one" goes to the supervisor. But run 1 again drops the three topic ideas (D7). Hard fail 4.

T10.title: Already well organised
T10.subtitle: Does it add anything?
T10.tests: The student has done the work. If the tool only reformats it, that is an honest finding.

notes.A1: Reformats a note that was already good. Adds little, harms nothing.
notes.B1: Faithful. The deadline placeholder is legitimate here: "timeline to submission" is in the note.
notes.B2: Faithful. Minor: "whether she wants to see ch4" is routed as institutional, so run 2's email cites a regulation for a supervisor preference.

S1.title: Early stage: scope not settled
S1.situation: First meeting after the topic was provisionally accepted. Has read widely, written nothing. Suspects the topic is too broad but cannot say why.
S1.issues: Question 2 mentions "a single case study", a term the student never used (D9). "I don't want to waste her time with stupid questions" is not acknowledged. The email reports "Opening: we formally opened the meeting" (D8).

S2.title: Mid thesis: the method is not working
S2.situation: Six weeks in. The survey got 14 of 80+ responses. Wants to switch to interviews but the methods chapter is already approved.
S2.issues: "Will it look like I didn't plan properly" became "academic integrity", which wrongly implies misconduct (D9). The student's three options are not extracted (D7). "Opening" lands fourth in the agenda (D8).

S3.title: Late stage: behind schedule
S3.situation: Eight weeks from submission, about three weeks behind. Has been avoiding the timeline conversation.
S3.issues: Good: no meeting length in the note, and none invented. But the reason for the meeting, "need to talk to her about the timeline", is not a concern, and the chapter status is unused (D7).

How many credits do I need before I can.expected: Answered from the documents, citing Art. 44.
How many credits do I need before I can.obs: Correct: 150 credits, Art. 44 cited, programme specifics included.

What happens if I fail the thesis - can.expected: Answered from the documents, with article numbers.
What happens if I fail the thesis - can.obs: Cites Art. 24, 27, 34, 43. One caution: it applies the general FX compensation rule to the thesis. The extract does not say whether that rule covers the thesis, so a student should check.

I might not be able to finish the thesis.expected: Answered from the documents, with article numbers.
I might not be able to finish the thesis.obs: Correct: notify the Studiengangleitung, written request, medical certificate (Art. 34).

When exactly is the submission deadline.expected: Refused: the documents do not say. Redirected to the official source.
When exactly is the submission deadline.obs: "This is not covered by the documents provided." No date or format guessed.

Is my research question specific enough.expected: Refused differently: no document can answer it; it is the supervisor's judgement.
Is my research question specific enough.obs: "A judgement that belongs to your supervisor." The two refusals stay distinct, which was the sharpest test in the project.
